FSSAI Seized 36 Tonnes Of Fake "Pure" Ghee In One City. Is The Jar In Your Kitchen Real?

Hint: the fake stuff now passes the smell test. Here is the one thing it can never fake.

Posted by the Eliqo Food Safety Desk

Right now, in a shed somewhere near your city, someone is heating palm oil and vanaspati over a flame. They stir in industrial colour and a flavour engineered to smell exactly like desi ghee. They pour it into a jar that says Pure. Premium. Farm Fresh. Then they sell it to you at a festive discount too good to walk past.

You carry it home. You warm it over your dal, spoon it onto your child's rice, stir it into the Diwali sweets your family has eaten for generations. And you never taste the difference. That is the entire point of the fraud.

Are you tired of trusting a jar you cannot actually verify?

The guessing. The second-guessing. The quiet worry every time another headline lands. If a small part of you has started to wonder whether any of it is real, keep reading. The headlines are worse than most people think.

Here's What's Really Inside A Lot Of "Pure" Ghee

This is not one rumour. It is the public record of the last three months, in three cities, from three sources you can open and read yourself.

India TodayHyderabad · 18 Aug 2026
36 tonnes of fake "desi" ghee seized in a single-city crackdown.Teams checked 130 outlets. The fakes were mixed from palm oil and vanaspati and sold under labels like "100% Pure." Some samples had no dairy at all.
Hindustan TimesDelhi · 2026
322 kg of unsafe ghee pulled from shops pushing discount reels.Delhi's Food Safety Department targeted stores advertising "buy one get one" and up to 60 percent off on social media.
PIB · FSSAI21 Aug 2026
FSSAI barred a maker's ghee after labs found plant fat in it.Sale of all its ghee was prohibited after samples showed beta-sitosterol, a marker of vegetable fat that has no place in ghee.

In Delhi, officials warned the seized fake ghee carried chemicals that can cause cancer. In the one fat you cook with every single day.

And you cannot smell it. The fakes are engineered to beat the exact test your grandmother taught you at the stove. The colour matches. The grain matches. The warm aroma matches. A lab has to hunt for a hidden plant fat to catch it. Your tongue never will.

6 In 10 Families No Longer Trust Their Ghee

6 in 10
Urban households say they do not trust the purity of the ghee they buy. Survey of more than 18,000 homes across 293 districts, July 2026.

You are not being difficult. You read the headlines and did the sensible thing: you got suspicious. The numbers say most of the country is right there with you.

Let's Start With The Label.

Every one of those seized fakes wore a beautiful word. 100% Pure. Natural. Farm Fresh. In Delhi they were even pushed through flashy discount reels, buy one get one, 60 percent off. The louder a jar shouts "pure," the less that word is worth. A word is not proof.

Kind Of Scary, Isn't It?

It should be. You are not cooking for strangers. You are cooking for the people you love most, every day, with something you assumed was safe. So what are you supposed to do? Stop cooking with ghee? Send every jar to a lab? Of course not. There is a simpler answer, and it is one question the fakes can never survive: "Can you show me the lab report for this exact batch?"
